findings.title: New SDK release report missing from the reports index
findings.message: The reports index adds the workbench-interaction, rendering and platform-support reports. It does not add the new docs/reports/sdk-release/README.md, although docs/implementation.md links to it. The SDK release evidence is therefore not reachable from the index, which this phase is updating to list the current reports.
findings.suggestion: Add a link to sdk-release/README.md in the reports index next to the other phase reports.

findings.title: Unlabeled older archive hash snapshot differs from the current one without provenance
findings.message: This file is a bare path-to-hash map with no archive_sha256, source commit, scope, digest_trust or final_source_tree_qualified fields. The sibling current-archive-source-hashes.json is labeled and hashes the same paths, but most of its hashes differ (building-an-app.md, contract_test.go, check-sdk.py, release-sdk.py, specs/release.md). A reader or tool cannot tell which archive or run this belongs to. It could be mistaken for current evidence, or for a contradiction of the current snapshot, when it is probably an earlier one.
findings.suggestion: Add the same metadata wrapper as current-archive-source-hashes.json (archive_sha256 or run identifier, source commit and clean flag, scope, historical/superseded status, and the final_source_tree_qualified false flag). Alternatively, rename the file to mark it as historical and reference it from the README.

findings.title: Verification and archive-parse failures bypass structured failure reporting
findings.message: Only subprocess.TimeoutExpired produces the structured check_failed event. Verification failures (ValueError), malformed archives (tarfile.HeaderError, gzip.BadGzipFile, EOFError, UnicodeDecodeError, JSON errors) and failed child commands (CalledProcessError) escape as raw tracebacks. A tool that consumes this JSON output gets inconsistent failure reporting. The malformed-archive errors are also not ValueError subclasses, so the checker's own validation errors are mixed with unexpected crashes.
findings.suggestion: Catch ValueError, tarfile.TarError, OSError, EOFError and CalledProcessError in main() and emit the same structured vellum.sdk.check_failed event with a non-zero exit.

findings.title: Zip external attributes depend on host filesystem modes, not normalized modes
findings.message: The Windows zip stores whatever mode `stat()` reports for each file. `normalize_layout` relies on POSIX `chmod`, which on a Windows host only toggles the read-only flag. The mode bits in the zip therefore vary by build host and do not match the normalized 0755/0644 used elsewhere. The archive is no longer reproducible across hosts, and the executable bit can be wrong when the archive is extracted on Unix-like systems.
findings.suggestion: Write explicit, host-independent modes into the zip (0o40755 for directories, 0o100755 for the .exe or any file with an exec bit, 0o100644 for other files) instead of reading `stat().st_mode`.

fix.after:
mode = 0o040755 if source.is_dir() else (0o100755 if source.suffix.lower() == ".exe" or source.stat().st_mode & 0o111 else 0o100644)
                record.external_attr = mode << 16

finding.title: Inconsistent Python check counts (52 vs 50) without explicit reconciliation
finding.message: The same README says the current unit results are fifty-two Python checks, then says the 'fresh' integrated gate passed all 50 SDK Python checks. The README only partly explains the chronology, so a reader cannot tell which count describes the current tree. Evidence counts that disagree without explanation weaken the audit trail.
finding.suggestion: State explicitly that integrated-check.txt was captured before two checks were added (50 at that moment, 52 now). Or label the 50 as historical rather than 'fresh'.
finding.evidence:
`integrated-check.txt` records the fresh complete local check gate passing all
50 SDK Python checks
